en: The President vetoes a bill passed by Congress, which forces legislators to gather a two-thirds vote to override the veto and enact the law.
The 1987 Constitution limits the Philippine President to a single six-year term, which prevents any leader from holding executive power indefinitely.
Displaying the Philippine flag with the red stripe on top signals a state of war, reversing the peacetime arrangement of the blue stripe.
The Ifugao people carve rice terraces into mountainsides, which creates stepped irrigation canals that channel rainwater down to sustain their crops.
Participants perform the two-steps-forward, one-step-back Sinulog dance, which mimics the flowing river current to visually honor the Santo Niño.
The barangay captain convenes the Lupong Tagapamayapa, which mediates neighborhood disputes locally to prevent minor conflicts from reaching the formal court system.
Jose Rizal wrote Noli Me Tangere and El Filibusterismo, which exposed the abuses of the Spanish friars and awakened Filipino national consciousness.
Registering as a voter with the COMELEC grants a citizen the legal right, and civic duty, to elect national and local officials.
The Surian ng Wikang Pambansa selected Tagalog as the basis for the national language, which unified the archipelago's diverse linguistic groups under one standardized tongue.
Dr. Fe del Mundo designed a bamboo incubator, which uses hot water in outer jars to maintain a steady temperature for premature babies during power outages.
A Filipino family practices pagmamano, which involves pressing an elder's hand to one's forehead to physically demonstrate respect and receive a blessing.
The Supreme Court exercises judicial review, which allows the justices to declare executive or legislative actions unconstitutional if they violate the 1987 Constitution.
